ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 through L.561-50 and R.561-1 through R.561-60; Article L.561-46 of the same Code (mandatory beneficial ownership declaration to the company registry); Decree No. 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 on beneficial ownership; Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (6th AML Directive); AMF General Regulation (Règlement général de l'AMF); Code de commerce Articles L.223-1 et seq. (SARL corporate governance); Public Health Code (Code de la santé publique) Articles L.5121-11 and L.5124-3 for pharmaceutical wholesale licensing; TRACFIN (French FIU) reporting obligations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (with restricted legitimate-interest access for obliged entities; general public access restricted by Constitutional Council decision No. 2022-1001 QPC of 11 July 2022)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate registration certificate and Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Administration for Market Regulation of the shareholder's domicile in the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China (effective for documents issued after 7 November 2023 upon China's accession to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961), followed by sworn French translation; consular legalization by a French Embassy is no longer required.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national identity document of each natural person shareholder and the proposed gérant (manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary office or Exit-Entry Administration of the competent Public Security Bureau in China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs) plus sworn translation by a court-approved expert translator registered with a French Cour d'appel.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal conviction (police clearance certificate) of the proposed gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Chinese court or notary office; supplemented after establishment by a French casier judiciaire extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs) if foreign-issued; the French casier judiciaire extract is obtained domestically and requires no apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each beneficial owner and the proposed gérant (utility bill or bank statement dated within three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn French translation; notarized attestation accepted as supporting evidence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and KYC compliance letter evidencing the source of funds for share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank legalization, Hague Apostille and sworn French translation; document must permit source-of-wealth verification under enhanced due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the incorporation agent and authorizing the gérant to sign incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs) plus sworn French translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of all apostilled Chinese corporate, identity, address and banking documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Traducteur expert près la Cour d'appel (court-approved sworn translator)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translation certified by the expert translator with the translator's official stamp and registry signature; no separate apostille is applied to the translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Executive form of SARL Articles of Association (statuts) either as a notarized deed or as an acte sous seing privé signed by all shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French civil-law notaire (if notarization elected) or licensed French avocat for the private deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for domestically executed deeds; the deed must bear the notaire's registration stamp where applicable and be filed through the INPI Guichet Unique.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all beneficial owners (at or above 25%), the gérant, and any authorized corporate signatories against the French national asset-freezing list (arrêtés of the Minister of the Economy), the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Regulation (EU) No 269/2014), the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the U.S. OFAC SDN list (applicable to USD-denominated Swift LC and bank wire transactions), and the FATF high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdictions list. PEP status is assessed pursuant to Article L.561-10-1 of the Code monétaire et financier and Decree No. 2018-284, with enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, senior-management approval, and TRACFIN suspicious transaction reporting triggered by the high-risk pharmaceutical API wholesale classification.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.notarization_doctrine_note: French law does not require notarization of SARL Articles of Association as a general rule; notarization is mandatory only when a contribution in kind involves immovable property or when a specific subsequent registered deed so requires. Foreign official documents serving as UBO and KYC evidence must be apostilled under the Hague Convention and professionally translated by a sworn translator.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique Electronique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) record verification via Infogreffe at infogreffe.fr; INSEE for SIREN/SIRET issuance; INPI trademark database search at bases-marques.inpi.fr.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All RCS filings and statutory documents must be drafted in French. A non-French dénomination sociale is permitted only if it is rendered in Latin-script transliteration and fully explained in the French text of the Articles of Association; misleading or non-transliterable terms are rejected. Every business document must display the French RCS identity block (including the legal form, registered office, RCS number and share capital) in accordance with Article R.123-237 of the Code de commerce; any foreign-language annex must be accompanied by a sworn French translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a reasoned refusal notice from the INPI Guichet Unique or the responsible greffe, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration (recours gracieux) within 30 calendar days, providing evidence of distinctiveness against existing RCS entries and compliance with French public policy and health-sector naming rules. A further judicial appeal lies before the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce by way of summary proceedings (référé) seeking an order to compel registration and damages for abusive refusal. In parallel, the applicant may lodge a distinctiveness challenge with INPI and re-file a fresh incorporation dossier after releasing the reserved name or submitting a modified compliant name; the procedural framework is found in Articles L.123-5 and R.123-30 of the Code de commerce.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A commercial domiciliation agreement under Article L.123-11-1 of the Code de commerce may validly serve as the SARL siège social for up to five years, but is not acceptable as the sole place of commercial substance for the licensed pharmaceutical API wholesale activity. The ANSM wholesale distribution licence requires a physically dedicated and GDP-compliant storage site approved after on-site inspection; therefore the corporate seat may be domiciliated while a separate licensed warehouse facility must be designated and operated in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High; estimated 85-95% probability of a mandatory pre-licensing ANSM inspection of the storage premises before the wholesale distribution licence becomes operative, with continued risk of unannounced inspections within six to eighteen months after licence issuance in accordance with ANSM Good Distribution Practice inspection policy.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border SARL incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation (traduction assermentée) of Chinese UBO, identity, address and KYC documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-approved sworn translator of a French Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per document and per page (EUR 25-60 per page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certification of the Chinese-origin document bundle (eight originals)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for end-to-end corporate formation project management

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II: Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (constitution, capital and management of SARL); Decree No. 84-406 on commercial registry (Articles R.123-1 et seq.); Law No. 2019-486 (PACTE) on the single window (guichet unique) formalities under Article L.123-6.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) acting through the INPI-operated single business formality window (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier unique de création (unified application) comprising the CERFA M0 declaration and annexed statutory instruments, filed electronically through the guichet unique of the INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL has no statutory minimum capital (may be as low as one euro). Under Article L.223-7 of the Commercial Code, cash contributions must be paid up to at least one-fifth at incorporation and the balance within five years. The subscribed funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account maintained by a French credit institution or a notary until the certificate of registration (Kbis) is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF [SARL NAME] (unanimous written decision). The undersigned founding shareholders, having reviewed the draft Articles of Association, hereby resolve as follows: 1. The Articles of Association are approved and signed by each member upon execution of this formal deed. Each member subscribes in full to the share capital set forth in Article 6 of the Articles. 2. The registered office is fixed at the address stated in Article 4, to remain until otherwise decided by an extraordinary general meeting. 3. All cash contributions are recorded and shall be remitted without delay into a blocked capital deposit account. 4. Mrs/Mr. [Name] is appointed as Gérant for an indefinite term and is authorized to open bank accounts, file the incorporation dossier, and complete all pre-registration steps. This resolution is effective upon signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders (self-executed private deed) or notary (when in-kind real estate contributions are made or when a minor is a shareholder).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French, enumerating cash and in-kind subscriptions, the identity of the gérant, the registered office, duration, and the corporate purpose covering wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients (ISIC 4649). Each shareholder signs the deed. In-kind contributions exceeding EUR 30,000 or representing more than 50% of share capital must be valued by a commissaire aux apports. Foreign shareholders must supply certified translations and legalised identity documents.
required_dossiers: Project of articles of association (statuts)
Proof of availability of registered office (lease, bail or ownership title)
Valid passport or national identity card of each shareholder
Commissaire aux apports valuation report (if in-kind contributions)
Certified French translation of any foreign corporate or personal documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry contests the corporate purpose clause or the deed language, amend the statuts by supplementary deed (acte rectificatif) and resubmit; constitutional defects may be cured within 30 days without nullifying the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital in Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (authorized bank) or notary receiving funds on behalf of the company in formation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account bearing the name of the SARL in formation and deposit at least 20% of each cash subscription. Obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds (bank certificate evidencing the blocking of funds). The funds are released solely upon presentation of the Kbis extract confirming registration or, failing registration within six months, on request of the subscribers.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts submitted to the bank officer
Subscriber list with capital apportionment
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (blocked funds certificate)
Statement of the five-year schedule for payment of the remaining 80% of contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate contains defects, obtain a corrected attestation with exact beneficiary wording; the capital may be redeposited and re-blocked with no penalty, provided the same subscribed amount is verified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice in an Authorized Gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) duly authorised by the prefecture of the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish an avis de constitution stating the company name, legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration and the names of the managers. Obtain the attestation de parution from the gazette. The unified incorporation filing must be submitted within eight days after publication of the notice.
required_dossiers: Approved statuts
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (if already issued)
Identity details of the appointed gérant
Exact corporate purpose clause for insertion in the notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette refuses publication due to an incomplete purpose clause, revise the clause and publish again; the eight-day filing deadline is recomputed from the date of the new publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Unified Electronic Incorporation Dossier (Guichet Unique)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic M0/CERFA equivalent declaration, selecting 'SARL' and the regulated activity 'distribution en gros de substances actives pharmaceutiques'. Attach the signed statuts, blocked-funds attestation, publication attestation, identity documents of the gérant and any preliminary reference from ANSM if already obtained. The platform forwards the dossier electronically to the competent Greffe and other administrations.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 declaration (déclaration de création d'entreprise)
Dated and signed statuts
Attestation de dépôt des fonds
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Déclaration sur l'honneur of the gérant regarding eligibility and absence of prohibitions
Copy of identity document of each gérant
Reference or copy of the initial ANSM authorisation file if the activity is launched immediately
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A 'dossier rejeté' notice is issued for illegible or missing attachments: cure by correcting the specific annex and resubmitting on the same portal; name conflicts are cured by adopting a new corporate name and re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Commercial Court Registry and Issuance of Kbis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce territorialement compétent (service de l'immatriculation du registre du commerce et des sociétés).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the validated dossier from the guichet unique, the greffier registers the SARL in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS). The registrar issues the original extrait Kbis constituting the legal existence certificate, together with the SIREN/SIRET numbers and the NAF code 4649Z. The VAT intra-community number is subsequently allocated by the competent tax office.
required_dossiers: Validated guichet unique dossier number
Original attestation de parution
Decision of the founding shareholders approving incorporation (first resolution)
Payment receipt of the greffe formalities fee
Proof of registered office premises if the registry requests an on-site verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe issues an observation requiring a supplementary document, provide the document within fifteen days; if the Kbis is delivered with errors, apply to the judge responsible for the registry for a rectification order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Regulated Pharmaceutical Wholesale Activity and Post-Registration Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM); URSSAF; local tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises); commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the definitive professional bank account, enrol the company with URSSAF, file the beneficial owner declaration in the register of beneficial owners, and lodge the ANSM application for authorisation to distribute active substances in bulk (Article L.5138-1 of the Code de la santé publique). No wholesale transaction may occur before the authorisation is granted and the premises satisfy good distribution practice (GDP) standards.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract issued less than three months prior
ANSM authorisation application file (CERFA and technical annexes)
Lease or ownership documents proving GDP-compliant storage premises
Beneficial owner declaration filed at the Greffe
Documented qualification and diplomas of the pharmaceutical compliance manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ANSM dossier is declared incomplete, respond within ten working days; if the agency fails to decide within ninety days, the application is deemed refused and an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Health within two months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM) — Direction des inspections et contrôles territoriaux.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation de distribution en gros de substances actives pharmaceutiques (authorisation for wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients under Articles L.5138-1 and R.5138-27 of the French Public Health Code).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) — Inspection des Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement, Ministry of Ecological Transition.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: 'Enregistrement' (registration) under ICPE rubrique 1510 only when dangerous substance storage thresholds are exceeded; for a pure wholesale and dry warehouse activity the installation is classified 'Non classé' and is exempt from a full environmental impact assessment report, subject to a simple waste-registration and self-monitoring declaration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Waste traceability under Article R.541-46 of the Environmental Code with a chronological waste register for expired or damaged pharmaceutical batches; volatile organic compound (VOC) limits in storage exhaust air below 20 mg/Nm3 pursuant to Directive 2016/2284; any process wastewater discharge declared under Article R.214-1 of the Environmental Code if daily volume exceeds 10 m3, with limits on COD below 2 g/m3 and pH between 5.5 and 8.5.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance issued after passage before the departmental consultative commission for safety and accessibility (CCDSA) with a favourable opinion of the fire brigade for premises exceeding 300 m2; structural stability inspection confirming load-bearing capacity of storage racks; occupational health clearance by the occupational health service with verification of workplace layout under Articles R.4214-1 et seq. of the Labour Code; periodic electrical installation inspection in accordance with NF C 15-100 with a three-year renewal cycle.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), operating under the Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances; official portal: impots.gouv.fr (professional access via 'Gérer mon entreprise'). Customs fiscal duties, export controls, and export valuation are administered separately by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI); official portal: douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned SARL: file incorporation through the single French business formalities desk (Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises, accessible at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr). The dossier generates the SIREN/SIRET identification numbers. The business court (Tribunal de Commerce / Greffe) issues the RCS extract, and the DGFiP automatically assigns the competent corporate tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises, SIE). The SARL must then submit VAT registration via the DGFiP form 3310 (option or compulsory registration) through impots.gouv.fr to obtain the French TVA number and, where applicable, the intra-Community VAT number. For customs export transactions, the company must additionally obtain an Economic Operator Registration and Identification (EORI) number from the DGDDI. The SARL is required to designate a day-to-day legal representative resident in France; where the shareholder is outside the EU, the DGFiP may require a statutory fiscal representative for indirect tax formalities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A French SARL is a capital company taxed by default at the level of the entity under the impôt sur les sociétés (IS) at the standard rate of 25% on worldwide profits (Article 206-1 CGI). Pass-through treatment is not automatic and is available only narrowly: a 'SARL de famille' satisfying Article 239 bis AA CGI, or a newly created small SARL meeting Article 239 bis AB CGI, may elect income-tax transparency in the hands of shareholders. For a wholesale distribution business dealing in pharmaceutical APIs, the practical and dominant default remains entity-level taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; entity classification is statutory. Available elections include: (i) the election under Article 239 bis AA/AB CGI for a qualifying SARL to be taxed like a partnership rather than at corporate level; (ii) the option for a VAT normal regime by a small operator benefiting from the franchise en base de TVA; (iii) the election to form a French group VAT entity under Article 267 CGI for closely controlled French subsidiaries; (iv) the election for fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) for French subsidiaries held directly or indirectly at 95% or more, allowing intra-group loss offset and transfer of tax attributes. Hybrid mismatch treatment under ATAD is mandatory and cannot be opted out; no elections are available to override anti-hybrid or exit-tax rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA). France applies no separate GST or general sales tax; VAT is the sole indirect tax on commercial goods and services, supplemented by specific excises and health-product duties where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France applies the EU small business exemption ('franchise en base de TVA'). For a wholesale trader of tangible goods such as pharmaceutical APIs, the standard VAT registration threshold is EUR 85,000 annual taxable turnover, with an upper tolerance of EUR 94,300 before registration becomes compulsory. Service activities use thresholds of EUR 37,500 and EUR 41,300 respectively. A French-established SARL conducting normal corporate accounting and wishing to recover input VAT has an unconditional right to elect for VAT registration below these thresholds. For intra-Community distance sales of goods, the harmonized EU threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year applies. A non-established foreign supplier has no turnover threshold: any taxable supply of goods or services in France requires a French VAT registration and a designated tax representative where the supplier is established outside the EU.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has adopted a mandatory B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting framework under Article 289 bis CGI. As currently legislated, French taxable persons must issue and receive structured electronic invoices and transmit transaction data to the DGFiP via the Public Invoice Platform (Portail Public de Facturation – PPF) or a certified private dematerialization platform (PDP): from 1 September 2026 for large and medium enterprises (grandes entreprises et ETI), and from 1 September 2027 for small enterprises and micro-enterprises. The mandatory formats are Factur-X (EN 16931), UBL, and CII. The system does not use Italian-style real-time fiscal stamping; integrity and legibility guarantees are required, and structured invoice data must be transmissible via interoperable APIs (Y1/Y2 flows) to the administration. For pharmaceutical API transactions, the invoice must contain the customs tariff code (CN), GTIN/product nomenclature where relevant, and the correct Incoterms to avoid mismatches between DGFiP e-reporting and DGDDI export declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A French SARL wholesale distributor of pharmaceutical APIs may apply the 0% VAT rate under Article 262-1 CGI exclusively where the goods are physically dispatched from France and leave the European Union customs territory, pursuant to an export customs declaration, to a buyer established outside the EU. The zero-rating is also available for intra-Community B2B supplies of goods to a purchaser holding a valid EU VAT number, subject to inclusion in the recapitulative statement (EC Sales List). For extra-EU exports, the following conditions are strictly cumulative: (i) the goods must actually depart from France without being consumed or resold in the EU; (ii) the exporter must hold documentary proof of the customs release and of the transport to a third-country destination; (iii) the commercial invoice must be issued to the foreign principal/customer and the payment must correspond to the export sale; and (iv) the exporter must keep the evidence readily available for DGFiP and DGDDI inspection. Wholesale supply of APIs to French hospitals, distributors, or pharmacies is domestic supply chargeable at 20% VAT; zero-rating cannot be applied merely on the basis of unverified resale or Commissaire de justice attestations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/Déclaration d'échange de biens with MRN customs release reference)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / CMR consignment note) naming the destination outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103 or bank credit advice documenting actual receipt of the export proceeds)
Commercial Invoice with exact API designation, ISIC/NAICS correspondence, CN tariff code, quantity, unit price and Incoterms

Transport and handling evidence (transport contract, weight/packing list, proof of dispatch from the French bonded facility) and, where applicable, ANSM/health authority export authorization or DGDDI pharmaceutical permit

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (within the Eurosystem and ESCB); external financial relations are administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor under the Code monétaire et financier; prudential supervision and AML enforcement are within the remit of the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully and freely convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions, subject only to the general safeguards permitted under Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. France imposes no prior FX authorisation or administrative quota for trade settlement, profit remittances, or capital injections on the capital account. Dividend remittance by a French SARL to a non-resident parent is unrestricted from an FX standpoint, though it remains subject to French corporate income tax, applicable withholding tax treaties, and CRS/FATCA reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion rule applies to export receipts in France. Exporters may lawfully retain foreign currency proceeds in authorised bank accounts within the EEA and are free to use them for working-capital or settlement purposes. Each cross-border payment is automatically captured by the resident credit institution for balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the Banque de France; physical export declarations must be lodged through the French Customs DELTA/DX system. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Corporate Operational Account (EUR/USD/CNY)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account, Trade Finance Line, and Foreign Exchange Clearing Account
Operational Account, Documentary Credit Facility, and Cash Management Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: low-to-medium. An Electronic Money Institution (EMI), whether French-licensed by the ACPR or passporting under PSD2, may provide payment accounts and money remittance but cannot lawfully take deposits, extend credit, issue documentary letters of credit, or guarantee trade instruments in France. For a high-risk pharmaceutical API wholesale business, EMIs offer practical one-click multi-currency collection but fail to meet the full settlement rails required for Swift LC operations and therefore should be considered a secondary or ancillary payment channel rather than a primary treasury banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banks interpret the ACPR anti-money-laundering rules strictly for a high-risk pharmaceutical distributor. A physical interview is effectively mandatory: the SARL’s gérant (managing director) and each ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more must appear at the bank’s compliance meeting in France or, exceptionally, before a French-regulated notary or ACPR-accredited video-identification agent. Remote-only onboarding is not accepted for a High-Risk_Special_License entity whose principal trade is cross-border API wholesale. The gérant must also provide a French business presence or designate a resident banking correspondent with a durable power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inadequate statutory authorisation for French pharmaceutical wholesale and API distribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Authorisation d’ouverture d’un établissement pharmaceutique issued by ANSM; wholesale distribution licence under Article L.5124-1 et seq. of the French Code de la santé publique; EU GTP/GDP certificate under the Falsified Medicines Directive; proof of a qualified pharmacist in charge; up-to-date ANSM registration and evidence of compliance with the obligation to report API flows to the national single portal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or multi-tier beneficial-ownership chain that prevents the bank from identifying the ultimate owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO chain from the SARL to each natural person, supported by an apostilled share register, corporate constitution documents for every intermediate holding entity, signed UBO declaration under Article R.561-1 of the Code monétaire et financier, tax-residence certificates of ultimate owners, audited financial statements of the SARL, and adverse-media screening results; sworn French translations of all non-French documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transactional patterns or counterparty concentrations suggestive of precursor diversion or sanctions circumvention.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each major purchase order: commercial invoice, certificate of analysis, bill of lading or airway bill, insurance certificate, transport contract, customs entry and export declarations from DELTA/DX data, and an EU Consolidated List / OFAC / UK sanctions screening report; written descriptive protocol demonstrating anti-diversion controls, product classification in CN/HTS code, and confirmation that no controlled precursor or dual-use goods subject to export authorisation are included.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unfavourable risk rating due to incorporation or residence of directors/UBOs in FATF black- or grey-listed jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Conclusive evidence of local economic substance: registered office lease in France, French payroll records, bank statements showing operating activity, minutes of board meetings held in France, and the SARL’s annual tax returns plus CRS/FATCA self-certifications for every shareholder; if required, formal remediation or segregation of such jurisdictions from the corporate treasury flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections must be wired to the French SARL’s blocked capital account through SEPA/TARGET2 if in EUR, or via SWIFT MT103 with cover through MT202 for USD/GBP/CNH. Use ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI (equity contribution) where provided; for shareholder intra-group loans use INTC. The receiving bank will quarantine the proceeds in a non-interest-bearing compte bloqué until the notarised deed of incorporation and the KYC defensive file are complete; the capital is thereafter released for operational use. No FX authorisation is required; however, the bank must submit a balance-of-payments statistical declaration to the Banque de France for any cross-border transaction, and foreign direct investment notifications to the Direction Générale du Trésor must be assessed where the pharma wholesale business touches sensitive-activity sectors or where sovereign rules impose prior authorisation thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational payments to API suppliers are executed by SWIFT MT103 for cross-currency funds, with correspondent clearing through major money-centre banks (e.g., Fedwire/CHIPS for USD, CIPS/offshore RMB for CNY, TARGET2 for intra-EUR payments). For bulk-API purchase contracts, the primary clearing rail is a commercial letter of credit under UCP 600: the French bank issues an MT700 through the SWIFT network to a nominated correspondent bank, against presentation of compliant shipping and insurance documents. Trade settlements should be routed exclusively via the French corporate bank account and not through cryptocurrency platforms or services that obscure the payment purpose. For export operations, payments can be collected using an MT103 inbound message with purpose code TRAD or INTC and documentary evidence retained for customs and tax audits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign exchange transactions against the ECB euro reference rate for immediate conversion of export receipts or supplier payments.
Outright forward exchange contracts (change à terme) with maturities up to 24 months, used to lock currency conversion on future USD, GBP, or CNY trade flows.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-deliverable currencies such as mainland CNH or INR indices where physical settlement is not available, provided the underlying trade exposure is marketable and documented.
Cross-currency swaps for term-mismatch hedging of FX cash flows on long-term API supply arrangements or intercompany financing.

European-style FX options and zero-cost collars (collar mechanisms) to cap unfavourable FX movement while preserving upside on favourable rate changes, exclusively for balance-sheet buyers and with no speculative leverage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approbation des comptes annuels — Annual general meeting (AGO) resolution approving financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed; corporate governance act recorded in the shareholders' minute book and delivered to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the INPI Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (calendar-year SARL: no later than 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered injunction on application of any interested party; €4,500 max judicial fine; managing director may be held liable for gérant negligence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels — Annual accounts (balance sheet, P&L, annexes) deposit at the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via INPI Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after AGO approval, i.e., by 31 July for calendar-year SARL with accounts approved by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial Court injunction with astreinte; court fine up to €4,500; failure to file for 3 consecutive years triggers regulatory strike-off (radiation) from the RCS, followed by judicial liquidation (clôture) of the entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) — UBO filing update and annual consistency verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via INPI Guichet unique (publicly accessible register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update within 30 days of any share transfer or beneficial ownership change; annual verification at the AGO meeting preceding the accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to €15,000 for legal entity and €7,500 for individuals (Art. L561-47 CMF); restrictions on bank transactions and disqualification from public tenders for non-filed or inaccurate RBE

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration de résultats IS — Form 2065-SD with 2050-series annexes (corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — electronic filing (EFI / impots.gouv.fr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day following 1 May (calendar-year SARL: typically 3 May); for non-calendar fiscal year, within 3 months of year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of assessed tax (up to 40% for deliberate failure); late-payment interest of 0.2% per month on tax due

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Solde de l'impôt sur les sociétés — Final balance payment of corporate income tax after annual assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP — via electronic transfer (TSA, SEPA direct debit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15 May (first business day following) for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-payment enforcement penalty on unpaid balance; 0.2% monthly late-payment interest; recovery by tax lien (avis à tiers détenteur)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) — Annual local business property tax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (local tax office, via form 1447-C-SD / pre-populated online return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment and declaration no later than 15 December for the current assessment year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing/late-payment penalty after formal notice; enforced recovery and seizure of business assets

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) mandatory if the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds at fiscal year-end: (i) balance sheet total > €4,000,000; (ii) net turnover excl. VAT > €8,000,000; (iii) average permanent workforce > 50 employees; audit is also compulsory for a SARL holding its pharmaceutical wholesale license if parent company consolidation requires it
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC Regulation 2016-07, CRC 99-02 for consolidated groups); IFRS as endorsed by the EU applies only to consolidated financial statements of listed groups

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France administers a Registers of Beneficial Owners (RBE) system filed at the Commercial Court Registry. Each share transfer or change in ownership > 25% of shares/voting rights or control must be declared on the RBE within 30 days; the gérant must annually confirm the RBE content matches the share ledger and the shares' transferability decisions at the AGO; no separate annual UBO filing is required unless a change occurred, but a consistency check is part of the annual accounts approval
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (share transfer/movement register)
Registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées et de décisions (shareholders' minute book)
Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs — RBE déclaration (registered beneficial owner file)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate; reduced rate of 15% applies to first €42,500 of profit for companies with annual turnover below €50 million)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII) may reduce effective rate for qualifying R&D activities, but wholesale distribution of APIs generally does not qualify. Tax losses can be carried forward indefinitely, but annual deduction is capped at €1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding that amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (and annexes 2065-A to 2065-SD) filed electronically via the EFI (Échange de Formulaires Informatifs) portal or the professional tax portal (impots.gouv.fr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending December 31, the return must be filed by the second business day after May 1st. For other fiscal year-ends, the deadline is within three months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (bénéfice imposable) after deduction of allowable expenses and prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must report French-source income only; allocate expenses proportionally and attach a statement of permanent establishment (if any).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward (déficits reportables) claimed against current-year profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses from French permanent establishments are eligible; provide supporting schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for tax credits (e.g., CIR, CII) and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim credits only if derived from French-source income and treaty provisions apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover and gross receipts (chiffre d'affaires) for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source turnover; attach a breakdown of cross-border transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing documentation declaration (Form 2257) if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with a French PE must file if cross-border related-party transactions exceed €150,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due, plus 0.5% per month of delay (capped at 10% of tax due). Interest at 0.2% per month applies. Additional penalties for failure to file electronically: €15 per form, up to €60 per form.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (domestic law rate; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the parent holds at least 10% for 2 years, or under applicable tax treaty rates, typically 0-15%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must submit a tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by its tax authority, along with Form 5000 (or Form 5001 for individuals) to the French tax administration. The reduced rate is applied at source if the TRC is provided before payment; otherwise, a refund claim must be filed within the statutory deadline (generally by December 31 of the second year following the income year).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 33.33%; reduced to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive (if beneficial owner is an EU company with ≥25% shareholding) or under tax treaties (typically 0-10%). Interest: statutory rate 30%; reduced under treaties (typically 0-10%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) is mandatory for companies with annual turnover or total assets exceeding €400 million. For smaller companies, a simplified documentation (Form 2257) is required if cross-border related-party transactions exceed €150,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but substance is critical for tax residency and anti-abuse rules. The General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) and the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) under tax treaties require genuine economic activity, including premises, employees, and decision-making in France. A shell company without substance risks denial of treaty benefits and recharacterization of transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false invoicing, or concealment of French-source profits in offshore accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Article 1741 CGI). Civil penalties: 40% to 80% of the evaded tax, plus interest at 0.2% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they participated in fraudulent acts. Travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition may apply. In severe cases, imprisonment up to 5 years and a ban on managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit with no real business activity, no employees, no physical office, or no local decision-making, while claiming treaty benefits or routing profits through France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of 25% withholding tax on deemed dividends. Administrative penalties up to 100% of the tax understated (Article 1729 CGI).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for the company's tax debts if they knowingly facilitated the sham structure. Travel bans and restrictions on leaving France may be imposed during tax investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining adequate records for high-risk pharmaceutical API transactions, including cash payments or opaque beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €5 million or 5% of annual turnover (Monetary and Financial Code). Criminal penalties for money laundering: up to 5 years imprisonment and €375,000 fine (Article 324-1 Penal Code).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned if they knowingly participate in or fail to prevent money laundering. Professional bans and confiscation of assets may apply.
